facts.activity_series: maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment
facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: unplanned release of chemical energy at TK-7102

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next field verification that the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip on TK-7102 and LT-7102 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically monitoring seal-face condition and temperature. TK-7102 (product storage tanks) is in service for export product storage. The task proceeded during transfer operations while the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip had degraded below its design intent. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 22 August 2012 a hazard report was recorded on TK-7102 and LT-7102 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during transfer operations; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
